title: Pipelined Credit Flow Control Buffer with Skid Register
description:
### Problem statement
High-performance on-chip networks decouple latency from throughput by coupling credit-based transmission with an internal skid buffer. The module tracks downstream credits (0..8) and can buffer up to 2 items locally (primary register and skid register). When `tx_req=1` and credit is available (`credits > 0`), the transmitter emits `tx_data` onto `tx_out` with `tx_valid=1` and decrements credits. Downstream returns credits via `credit_ret=1`. If downstream stalls (`m_ready=0`), incoming items skid safely into the auxiliary register without dropping words.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_credit_skid_buf(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       credit_ret,
    input  logic       tx_req,
    input  logic [7:0] tx_data,
    output logic       tx_valid,
    output logic [7:0] tx_out,
    output logic [3:0] credit_count,
    output logic       skid_active
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register `credit_count` initializes to 4'd4 on async `rst_n`.
- When `credit_ret=1` and no send: increment `credit_count <= credit_count + 1` (max 8).
- When `tx_req=1` and `credit_count > 0`:
  - If `credit_ret=0`: assert `tx_valid=1`, `tx_out <= tx_data`, `credit_count <= credit_count - 1`.
  - If `credit_ret=1`: assert `tx_valid=1`, `tx_out <= tx_data`, `credit_count` unchanged.
- If `tx_req=1` but `credit_count == 0`: deassert `tx_valid=0`, assert `skid_active <= 1`, hold `tx_out`.
- When credits become available, `skid_active <= 0`.
- `rst_n` resets outputs to 0 (credits to 4).

#### Notes
Credit flow coupled with local skid elasticity prevents head-of-line blocking in multi-hop routers.

module sv_x_credit_skid_buf(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       credit_ret,
    input  logic       tx_req,
    input  logic [7:0] tx_data,
    output logic       tx_valid,
    output logic [7:0] tx_out,
    output logic [3:0] credit_count,
    output logic       skid_active
);
    // TODO: implement credit-managed transmission with stall buffer

endmodule
solution_hints: Initialize credit_count to 4 on reset.
Transmit occurs only if tx_req is high and credit_count > 0.
skid_active asserts when tx_req is asserted but credits are exhausted.

title: Four-Channel Deficit Round-Robin (DRR) Packet Scheduler
description:
### Problem statement
Deficit Round-Robin provides fair bandwidth allocation across queues with variable packet lengths. In each round, an active queue receives a quantum of credits (`quantum = 4'd4`). If its pending packet cost `pkt_cost [3:0]` is <= its deficit counter, it transmits (`grant=1`), and its deficit counter decrements by `pkt_cost`. If cost exceeds deficit, the queue holds its deficit for the next round and the scheduler moves to the next active queue.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_drr_scheduler(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] queue_active,
    input  logic [3:0] pkt_cost,
    output logic [1:0] cur_queue,
    output logic       grant,
    output logic [3:0] deficit_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous scheduler rotating among active queues 0..3.
- When rotating to an active queue: add quantum 4 to its internal deficit counter.
- If `pkt_cost <= deficit`: assert `grant=1`, decrement deficit by `pkt_cost`.
- Else: `grant=0`, advance `cur_queue` to next active queue.
- `deficit_out` outputs the deficit counter of `cur_queue`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
DRR achieves O(1) scheduling complexity while guaranteeing fair long-term bandwidth shares.
starter_code:
module sv_x_drr_scheduler(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] queue_active,
    input  logic [3:0] pkt_cost,
    output logic [1:0] cur_queue,
    output logic       grant,
    output logic [3:0] deficit_out
);
    // TODO: implement 4-queue deficit round-robin quantum scheduler

endmodule
solution_hints: Maintain an array logic [3:0] deficit [0:3] for the 4 queues.
Add quantum 4 when visiting a queue for its service slice.
Grant if pkt_cost <= deficit; otherwise leave deficit intact and advance to next queue.

title: Fix: Pipelined Carry-Save Multiplier Accumulator Stage
description:
### Problem statement
Carry-Save Adders (CSA) avoid carry propagation by outputting redundant Sum and Carry vectors: `sum = a ^ b ^ c` and `carry = (a & b) | (b & c) | (a & c)`. The starter module implements a registered 3-operand CSA stage. However, it accidentally shifts the `carry` vector left by 2 positions instead of 1 position (`carry <= {c_out, 1'b0}`), corrupting the arithmetic product! Fix the carry shift alignment.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_csa_mac_fix(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [7:0] op_a,
    input  logic [7:0] op_b,
    input  logic [7:0] op_c,
    output logic [7:0] sum_out,
    output logic [7:0] carry_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure synchronous CSA stage registering sum and carry vectors on posedge clk.
- Bitwise sum: `sum_next = op_a ^ op_b ^ op_c`.
- Bitwise carry generation: `c_gen = (op_a & op_b) | (op_b & op_c) | (op_a & op_c)`.
- Alignment: Carry represents weight 2^(i+1), so `carry_next = {c_gen[6:0], 1'b0}`.
- At posedge clk: `sum_out <= sum_next`, `carry_out <= carry_next`.
- `rst_n` clears `sum_out` and `carry_out` to 0.

#### Notes
Carry vectors in CSA must shift left by exactly 1 position to maintain positional weight.
solution_hints: Examine carry_out registration inside always_ff.
Carry out bit i carries into bit position i+1.
Correct shift expression to {carry_comb[6:0], 1'b0}.

title: Implement the Timing: Non-Blocking AXI4-Lite Slave Register Slice
description:
### Problem statement
An AXI4-Lite slave register slice terminates read address (`ar`) and read data (`r`) channels without combinational feedthrough. On `arvalid=1`, it accepts address `araddr` by asserting `arready=1` for one cycle, fetches data from internal register bank (Address 0 -> `8'h11`, Address 1 -> `8'h22`, Address 2 -> `8'h33`, Address 3 -> `8'h44`), asserts `rvalid=1` on the next cycle, and holds until `rready=1`. Implement the timing specified in the table.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_axil_slave_slice(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       arvalid,
    input  logic [1:0] araddr,
    output logic       arready,
    output logic       rvalid,
    output logic [7:0] rdata,
    input  logic       rready
);
```

#### Requirements
- State machine: S_IDLE -> S_DATA.
- In S_IDLE: `arready=1`, `rvalid=0`. When `arvalid=1`: sample `araddr`, latch corresponding ROM data into `rdata`, move to S_DATA.
- In S_DATA: `arready=0`, `rvalid=1`. When `rready=1`: return to S_IDLE.
- ROM data: 0->17 (`8'h11`), 1->34 (`8'h22`), 2->51 (`8'h33`), 3->68 (`8'h44`).
- `rst_n` asynchronously resets to S_IDLE with outputs 0 (arready=1).

#### Notes
Register slices decouple timing paths on both master and slave sides of the interface.

title: Checker: FIFO Gray Pointer Multi-Bit CDC Jump Guard
description:
### Problem statement
In clock domain crossing (CDC) FIFOs, pointers sent across clock boundaries must be Gray coded so that exactly one bit changes between successive values (Hamming distance == 1). A multi-bit jump indicates clock domain metastability or sampling corruption. This checker computes `hamming_dist = popcount(gray_in ^ last_gray)`. If `hamming_dist > 1`, it immediately asserts `cdc_jump_err=1`. If pointers hold (`dist == 0`) or step by 1 (`dist == 1`), `cdc_jump_err=0`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_gray_cdc_checker(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] gray_in,
    output logic [2:0] hamming_dist,
    output logic       cdc_jump_err
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous monitor on posedge clk.
- Register `last_gray <= gray_in`.
- Compute difference `diff = gray_in ^ last_gray`.
- Population count `pop = diff[0] + diff[1] + diff[2] + diff[3]`.
- At posedge clk: `hamming_dist <= pop`, `cdc_jump_err <= (pop > 1)`.
- `rst_n` initializes `last_gray=0`, outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Gray pointer invariants form the fundamental safety proof in formal CDC verification.
solution_hints: XOR current gray_in with last_gray register.
Compute popcount of the 4-bit difference.
Assert cdc_jump_err when popcount exceeds 1.

title: Asymmetric Width Dual-Clock FIFO Pointer Synchronizer
description:
### Problem statement
In asymmetric FIFOs where the write side is 8 bits and read side is 16 bits (1:2 ratio), write pointers advance by 1 while read pointers advance by 2 byte positions per operation. Both pointers must be aligned to byte-granularity 4-bit addresses (0..15). When `wr_en=1`, `wr_ptr` increments by 1. When `rd_en=1`, `rd_ptr` increments by 2. The module calculates available words in 16-bit format `words_16bit = (wr_ptr - rd_ptr) >> 1` and produces `empty` and `full` flags.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_asym_fifo_ptrs(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       wr_en,
    input  logic       rd_en,
    output logic [3:0] wr_ptr,
    output logic [3:0] rd_ptr,
    output logic [2:0] words_16bit,
    output logic       empty,
    output logic       full
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous pointer updates on posedge clk.
- Byte occupancy `byte_occ = wr_ptr - rd_ptr` (4-bit modular subtraction).
- `words_16bit = byte_occ[3:1]` (division by 2).
- `empty = (byte_occ < 4'd2)` (cannot read a full 16-bit word).
- `full = (byte_occ >= 4'd14)` (cannot accept 2 more bytes).
- Advance `wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1` if `wr_en && !full`.
- Advance `rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 2` if `rd_en && !empty`.
- `rst_n` clears pointers to 0.

#### Notes
Asymmetric width FIFOs perform word packing and unpacking directly within FIFO address logic.

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       wr_en,
    input  logic       rd_en,
    output logic [3:0] wr_ptr,
    output logic [3:0] rd_ptr,
    output logic [2:0] words_16bit,
    output logic       empty,
    output logic       full
);
    // TODO: implement 1:2 asymmetric width FIFO pointer manager

endmodule
solution_hints: Calculate byte occupancy wr_ptr - rd_ptr.
A read requires at least 2 bytes (empty = byte_occ < 2).
wr_ptr increments by 1; rd_ptr increments by 2.

title: Priority Arbiter with Configurable Grant Holding and Aging
description:
### Problem statement
A 2-master bus arbiter balances latency and efficiency using grant holding and age boosting. Once a master wins grant (`grant0` or `grant1`), it retains the grant as long as its request remains high, up to a maximum hold limit `hold_limit = 2'd2` cycles. While Master 0 holds the grant, if Master 1 requests continuously for 2 cycles, Master 1's age elevates, forcing grant preemption at the end of the hold window.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_aging_arbiter(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic req0,
    input  logic req1,
    output logic grant0,
    output logic grant1,
    output logic [1:0] hold_cnt
);
```

#### Requirements
- Default priority: `req0 > req1`.
- When granted, `hold_cnt` counts consecutive cycles holding the grant (0..2).
- If granted master keeps request high and `hold_cnt < 2`: hold grant, increment `hold_cnt`.
- If `hold_cnt == 2` and the other master is requesting: switch grant to the other master, reset `hold_cnt <= 0`.
- If current master releases request: grant immediately passes to requesting master; `hold_cnt <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Grant holding amortizes bus setup overhead while hold caps guarantee latency bounds.

    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic req0,
    input  logic req1,
    output logic grant0,
    output logic grant1,
    output logic [1:0] hold_cnt
);
    // TODO: implement hold-limited priority arbiter

endmodule
solution_hints: Track active master (0 or 1) and hold counter.
Increment hold_cnt while the same master retains grant.
Preempt when hold_cnt reaches 2 and competing request is active.

title: Fix: Restoring Fixed-Point Square Root Rounding Bug
description:
### Problem statement
A fixed-point square root core computes the 4-bit integer square root of an 8-bit radicand `val_in` with round-to-nearest integer rounding. If remainder `rem >= root`, the integer root should round up (`root_rounded = root + 1`). The starter code has an erroneous inverted check `if (rem < root) root_rounded = root + 1;`, which rounds down on large remainders and rounds up on small remainders! Fix the rounding condition.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_fixed_sqrt_fix(
    input  logic [7:0] val_in,
    output logic [3:0] root_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- Compute exact integer square root `r = floor(sqrt(val_in))`.
- Compute exact remainder `rem = val_in - (r * r)`.
- If `rem >= r`: `root_out = r + 4'd1` (round to nearest).
- Else: `root_out = r`.

#### Notes
Round-to-nearest prevents systematic DC bias in digital demodulators.
solution_hints: Check the rounding branch condition.
Rounding up occurs when remainder is at least as large as the root (rem >= r).
Replace rem < {4'd0, r} with rem >= {4'd0, r}.

title: Implement the Timing: Synchronous Serial CRC-32 Ethernet Engine
description:
### Problem statement
IEEE 802.3 Ethernet CRC-32 computes remainder with polynomial `32'h04C11DB7`. The LFSR initializes to `32'hFFFFFFFF` on `init=1`. On each clock cycle with `data_valid=1`, serial bit `data_bit` updates the LFSR: `fb = crc_reg[31] ^ data_bit`; if `fb=1`, `crc_reg <= {crc_reg[30:0], 1'b0} ^ 32'h04C11DB7`, else shifts left. When frame ends, `crc_valid` asserts presenting the top byte `crc_byte = ~crc_reg[31:24]`. Implement the timing specified in the table.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_crc32_serial_engine(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       init,
    input  logic       data_valid,
    input  logic       data_bit,
    output logic [7:0] crc_byte,
    output logic       crc_valid
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register `crc_reg` initializes to `32'hFFFFFFFF` when `init=1`.
- Update with polynomial `32'h04C11DB7` on each `data_valid=1`.
- Output `crc_byte = ~crc_reg[31:24]` (inverted MSB byte per Ethernet spec).
- Assert `crc_valid=1` when `data_valid=0` after at least 1 valid bit processed.
- `rst_n` resets `crc_reg` to `32'hFFFFFFFF`, outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Ethernet inverts the final remainder to ensure zero-stuffed packets generate non-zero check sequences.

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       init,
    input  logic       data_valid,
    input  logic       data_bit,
    output logic [7:0] crc_byte,
    output logic       crc_valid
);
    // TODO: implement Ethernet CRC-32 serial bit engine

endmodule
solution_hints: Maintain 32-bit LFSR crc_reg initialized to 32'hFFFFFFFF.
Feedback bit is crc_reg[31] ^ data_bit.
Invert top byte (~crc_reg[31:24]) for Ethernet standard output byte.

title: Checker: AXI-Stream Backpressure Deadlock Latency Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
AXI-Stream backpressure must not persist indefinitely. If a consumer asserts `tvalid=1` but `tready` remains `0` for more than `max_stall = 3'd4` consecutive clock cycles, an interconnect deadlock has occurred. This verification monitor asserts `deadlock_err=1` and registers `stall_duration`. The alarm resets when the consumer asserts `tready=1` or `tvalid` deasserts.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_axis_deadlock_checker(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       tvalid,
    input  logic       tready,
    output logic [2:0] stall_duration,
    output logic       deadlock_err
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous registered monitor on posedge clk.
- If `tvalid && !tready`:
  - If `stall_duration < 4`: increment `stall_duration <= stall_duration + 1`, `deadlock_err <= 0`.
  - If `stall_duration >= 4`: hold `stall_duration <= 4`, assert `deadlock_err <= 1`.
- If `tready || !tvalid`: clear `stall_duration <= 0`, `deadlock_err <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Deadlock monitors locate stalled routers in complex Network-on-Chip meshes.
solution_hints: Increment stall_duration when tvalid is high and tready is low.
Cap stall_duration at 4 to prevent rollover.
Assert deadlock_err when stall_duration reaches 4.

title: Two-Way Set-Associative Cache Directory with Pseudo-LRU Replacement
description:
### Problem statement
A 2-way set-associative cache line directory stores two 6-bit tags per set (Way 0 and Way 1) along with a 1-bit LRU bit (`lru=0` indicates Way 0 was least recently used and is next candidate for replacement). When `lookup=1`, the directory checks if `tag_in` matches either valid way (`hit=1`, `hit_way`). If a hit occurs, `lru` updates to point to the other way. If a miss occurs (`hit=0`) and `allocate=1`, the missing tag overwrites the way indicated by `lru`, and `lru` updates.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_cache_lru_dir(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       lookup,
    input  logic       allocate,
    input  logic [5:0] tag_in,
    output logic       hit,
    output logic       hit_way,
    output logic       lru_way,
    output logic [5:0] way0_tag,
    output logic [5:0] way1_tag
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register tags `way0_tag`, `way1_tag`, valid bits `v0`, `v1`, and `lru_bit` (0->Way 0, 1->Way 1).
- Hits: `hit0 = v0 && (way0_tag == tag_in)`, `hit1 = v1 && (way1_tag == tag_in)`.
- Output `hit = hit0 || hit1`, `hit_way = hit1`, `lru_way = lru_bit`.
- LRU updates at posedge clk: if hit0, `lru_bit <= 1`; if hit1, `lru_bit <= 0`.
- Allocation on miss: if `allocate && !hit`: if `lru_bit==0`, `way0_tag <= tag_in, v0 <= 1, lru_bit <= 1`; else `way1_tag <= tag_in, v1 <= 1, lru_bit <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears valid bits and tags to 0, `lru_bit=0`.

#### Notes
LRU replacement minimizes cache miss rates for temporal locality workloads.

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       lookup,
    input  logic       allocate,
    input  logic [5:0] tag_in,
    output logic       hit,
    output logic       hit_way,
    output logic       lru_way,
    output logic [5:0] way0_tag,
    output logic [5:0] way1_tag
);

endmodule

lru_bit tracks the replacement victim (0 for way0, 1 for way1).
Update lru_bit upon access or allocation to point to the other way.

title: Two-Level Weighted Round-Robin Arbiter with Dynamic Burst
description:
### Problem statement
A network switch arbitrates between High-Bandwidth Master 0 (weight 2) and Standard Master 1 (weight 1). When both request simultaneously, Master 0 receives grants for 2 consecutive cycles before Master 1 receives 1 grant cycle (2:1 ratio). If a master has no pending request, the arbiter immediately serves the other master without wasting idle cycles. Output `active_master` indicates current grant.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_wrr_burst_arbiter(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic req0,
    input  logic req1,
    output logic grant0,
    output logic grant1,
    output logic [1:0] weight_cnt
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 2:1 weighted arbiter on posedge clk.
- Counter `weight_cnt` counts grants given to Master 0 (0..2).
- If both request (`req0 && req1`):
  - If `weight_cnt < 2`: grant Master 0 (`grant0=1, grant1=0`), increment `weight_cnt`.
  - If `weight_cnt == 2`: grant Master 1 (`grant0=0, grant1=1`), reset `weight_cnt <= 0`.
- If only `req0`: grant Master 0, increment/hold `weight_cnt` (cap at 2).
- If only `req1`: grant Master 1, reset `weight_cnt <= 0`.
- If neither: `grant0=0, grant1=0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Weighted Round-Robin arbiters guarantee proportional service rates without complex division.

title: Fix: Run-Length Stream Decompressor Buffer Underflow
description:
### Problem statement
An RLE decompressor accepts compressed tokens containing a 4-bit symbol `sym_in` and a 4-bit repetition count `len_in` (1..15) with `token_valid=1`. It repeats `sym_in` on `data_out` for `len_in` clock cycles with `data_valid=1`. The starter code has an off-by-one counter bug: it decrements the run counter BEFORE checking zero, causing it to emit `len_in - 1` items instead of `len_in` items! Fix the repetition counter logic.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_rle_decompress_fix(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       token_valid,
    input  logic [3:0] sym_in,
    input  logic [3:0] len_in,
    output logic       token_ready,
    output logic       data_valid,
    output logic [3:0] data_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous state machine on posedge clk.
- When IDLE (`rem_len == 0`):
  - `token_ready = 1`.
  - When `token_valid=1`: latch `sym_in` into `cur_sym`, set `rem_len <= len_in`, assert `data_valid <= 1`, `data_out <= sym_in`.
- While running (`rem_len > 1`):
  - `token_ready = 0`, `data_valid = 1`, `data_out = cur_sym`, `rem_len <= rem_len - 1`.
- On final item (`rem_len == 1`): `rem_len <= 0`, `token_ready <= 1`.
- `rst_n` resets all registers and outputs to 0 (`token_ready=1`).

#### Notes
Decompression off-by-one errors cause byte-misalignment in compressed pixel buffers.
solution_hints: Latching len_in - 1 causes the run to terminate one cycle too early.
Set rem_len <= len_in on token load.
token_ready goes high when rem_len <= 1.

title: Implement the Timing: Delta-Sigma Second-Order Noise Shaper
description:
### Problem statement
A second-order delta-sigma modulator achieves 40 dB/decade noise shaping using two cascaded accumulators. An 8-bit input `din` enters Accumulator 1: `acc1 <= acc1 + din - (bit_out ? 255 : 0)`. Accumulator 2 integrates Accumulator 1: `acc2 <= acc2 + acc1 - (bit_out ? 255 : 0)`. When `acc2[8]` overflows, output pulse `bit_out=1`. Implement the timing specified in the table.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_deltasigma_order2(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [7:0] din,
    output logic       bit_out,
    output logic [7:0] acc1_out,
    output logic [7:0] acc2_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 2-stage accumulator on posedge clk.
- Compute feedback subtraction: `fb = bit_out ? 8'd255 : 8'd0`.
- Acc1 update: `acc1 <= acc1 + din - fb`.
- Acc2 update: `acc2 <= acc2 + acc1 - fb`.
- Bit output: `bit_out <= (acc2 >= 8'd128)`.
- `acc1_out <= acc1`, `acc2_out <= acc2`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers and outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Second-order modulators push quantization distortion deep into out-of-band high frequencies.
solution_hints: Use two 8-bit registers acc1 and acc2.
Subtract 255 feedback when bit_out was asserted on the previous cycle.
Drive bit_out high whenever acc2 >= 128.

title: Checker: Mutex Grant Token Loss and Re-Seeding Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
In a distributed token ring arbiter with 4 nodes, exactly one token bit must circulate across `token_ring [3:0]` at all times (`popcount(token_ring) == 1`). If a cosmic ray or transient glitch causes token loss (`token_ring == 4'b0000`) for 2 consecutive cycles, the monitor asserts `token_lost_err=1` and pulses `reseed_token=1` to inject a fresh token at Node 0. If multiple tokens appear (`popcount > 1`), `duplicate_token_err=1` asserts.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_token_loss_checker(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] token_ring,
    output logic       token_lost_err,
    output logic       duplicate_token_err,
    output logic       reseed_token
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous verification monitor on posedge clk.
- Population count `pop = token_ring[0] + token_ring[1] + token_ring[2] + token_ring[3]`.
- If `pop > 1`: assert `duplicate_token_err <= 1`, clear `token_lost_err <= 0`, `reseed_token <= 0`.
- If `pop == 0`: increment lost timer. When lost timer reaches 2: assert `token_lost_err <= 1`, assert `reseed_token <= 1`.
- If `pop == 1`: clear error flags and lost timer.
- `rst_n` clears all error flags and timer to 0.

#### Notes
Self-healing token monitors restore liveness in distributed fault-tolerant topologies.
solution_hints: Compute popcount of token_ring.
Flag duplicate_token_err immediately when popcount > 1.
Count cycles with popcount == 0 to trigger token_lost_err and reseed_token.

title: Pipelined Booth Radix-4 Multiplier Step Slice
description:
### Problem statement
Radix-4 Modified Booth Encoding halves the number of partial products by inspecting 3 overlapping multiplier bits `{b[2i+1], b[2i], b[2i-1]}`. The recoded operation on multiplicand `M` produces: `0 -> 0`, `1,2 -> +M`, `3 -> +2M`, `4 -> -2M`, `5,6 -> -M`, `7 -> 0`. This pipeline slice accepts multiplicand `m_in [7:0]` and 3-bit window `b_window [2:0]`, computes the selected partial product, and registers the 9-bit signed partial product `pp_out` on posedge clk.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_booth_radix4_slice(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [7:0] m_in,
    input  logic [2:0] b_window,
    output logic [8:0] pp_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous Booth recoder registered on posedge clk.
- Encoding table for `b_window`:
  - 3'b000, 3'b111: `pp_next = 9'sd0`
  - 3'b001, 3'b010: `pp_next = {m_in[7], m_in}` (+1M)
  - 3'b011: `pp_next = {m_in, 1'b0}` (+2M)
  - 3'b100: `pp_next = ~{m_in, 1'b0} + 9'sd1` (-2M)
  - 3'b101, 3'b110: `pp_next = ~{m_in[7], m_in} + 9'sd1` (-1M)
- At posedge clk: `pp_out <= pp_next`.
- `rst_n` clears `pp_out` to 0.

#### Notes
Radix-4 Booth encoding cuts multiplier tree depth and routing congestion in half.
solution_hints: Sign-extend m_in to 9 bits: logic [8:0] m_ext = {m_in[7], m_in}.
Negative products are two's complement: (~val + 1).
Map each of the 8 3-bit window patterns to 0, +M, +2M, -2M, -M.

title: Packet Parser with Dynamic TLV Field Extraction
description:
### Problem statement
A network protocol carries options as Type-Length-Value (TLV) triples. Each TLV begins with Tag byte `tag_in` (8-bit), followed by Length `len_in` (1..2 bytes), followed by the payload value. This parser extracts Tag 8'h01 (Payload length 1 byte -> `opt_a_val`) and Tag 8'h02 (Payload length 1 byte -> `opt_b_val`). When a target option completes, `opt_valid` pulses with the option ID (`1` for A, `2` for B). If an unknown tag appears, it skips the length payload and continues.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_tlv_packet_parser(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       byte_valid,
    input  logic [7:0] byte_in,
    output logic [1:0] opt_id,
    output logic [7:0] opt_val,
    output logic       opt_valid
);
```

- In S_TAG: on `byte_valid=1`, store `tag <= byte_in`, move to S_LEN.
- In S_LEN: on `byte_valid=1`, store `len <= byte_in`, move to S_VAL.
- In S_VAL: on `byte_valid=1`, if `tag == 8'h01`, assert `opt_valid=1, opt_id=1, opt_val=byte_in`; if `tag == 8'h02`, assert `opt_valid=1, opt_id=2, opt_val=byte_in`. Return to S_TAG.
- When not in matching VAL, `opt_valid=0`.
- `rst_n` clears state to S_TAG, outputs to 0.

title: Fix: Watchdog Early-Pet Race Condition under Burst Resets
description:
### Problem statement
A safety watchdog counts up to `timeout = 4'd8`. It permits petting only when `count >= 4'd4`. If `pet=1` occurs when `count < 4`, it flags an illegal early pet (`early_err=1`). The starter code has a race condition: when `pet` arrives at the exact cycle `count == 4`, it evaluates `count < 4` using the NEXT counter value instead of the current registered value, triggering false `early_err` faults! Fix the registered evaluation order.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_watchdog_race_fix(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       pet,
    output logic [3:0] count,
    output logic       early_err,
    output logic       timeout_err
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous watchdog counter on posedge clk.
- If `pet=1`:
  - If current `count < 4`: assert `early_err <= 1`, clear `count <= 0`.
  - Else: `early_err <= 0`, clear `count <= 0`.
- Else if `count >= 8`: assert `timeout_err <= 1`, hold `count <= 8`.
- Else: `count <= count + 1`, `early_err <= 0`, `timeout_err <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers and outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Boundary condition evaluation order between concurrent counter increments and strobe inputs must be strictly deterministic.
solution_hints: Examine the check inside if (pet).
A pet is legal when count >= 4 (illegal only when count < 4).
Change if (count <= 4'd4) to if (count < 4'd4).

title: Implement the Timing: Bitstream Deserializer with Elastic Skid FIFO
description:
### Problem statement
A serial receiver deserializes 4-bit nibbles from `sin` when `sin_valid=1`. Upon assembling a complete 4-bit nibble, it transfers it to a 2-deep elastic buffer. Downstream reads bytes from the buffer using `m_ready=1`. If downstream stalls (`m_ready=0`), the elastic buffer holds up to 2 assembled nibbles before asserting `overflow_err=1`. ```

title: Pipelined CORDIC Vector Rotation Elementary Stage
description:
### Problem statement
A single stage in an unrolled CORDIC rotation pipeline performs an elementary coordinate rotation by elementary angle constant `angle_lut [7:0]`. When direction bit `dir=0` (clockwise), the coordinates update as `x_next = x - (y >> shift)`, `y_next = y + (x >> shift)`, and angle accumulator `z_next = z - angle_lut`. When `dir=1` (counter-clockwise), `x_next = x + (y >> shift)`, `y_next = y - (x >> shift)`, and `z_next = z + angle_lut`. All signals are registered synchronously on `clk`.

#### Module interface

```systemverilog
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       dir,
    input  logic [2:0] shift,

    input  logic [7:0] x_in,

    input  logic [7:0] z_in,

    output logic [7:0] z_out
);
```

- If `dir == 0`: `x_out <= x_in - y_sh`, `y_out <= y_in + x_sh`, `z_out <= z_in - angle_lut`.
- If `dir == 1`: `x_out <= x_in + y_sh`, `y_out <= y_in - x_sh`, `z_out <= z_in + angle_lut`.

title: Sequential Restoring Divider Datapath
description:
### Problem statement
A sequential 4-bit unsigned divider computes quotient `q` and remainder `r` of an 8-bit dividend `dividend [7:0]` divided by 4-bit divisor `divisor [3:0]`. When `start=1`, the engine loads operands and asserts `busy=1`. Over 8 successive clock cycles, the accumulator shifts left and subtracts the divisor. If the difference is non-negative, the quotient bit is set to 1; otherwise, the remainder is restored and the bit is 0. On the 8th cycle, `busy` deasserts and `done` pulses high with valid `quotient` and `remainder`.

#### Module interface

```systemverilog
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic [7:0] dividend,
    input  logic [3:0] divisor,
    output logic [7:0] quotient,

);
```

title: Two-Master to Two-Slave Memory Crossbar Switch
description:
### Problem statement
A 2x2 crossbar switch routes requests from Master 0 and Master 1 to Memory Bank 0 and Bank 1. Each master supplies a valid request `req_m [1:0]`, target destination bank `dest_m0, dest_m1`, and write data `wdata_m0, wdata_m1 [7:0]`. If both masters target different banks, both requests proceed simultaneously. If both target the same bank, Master 0 has priority, and Master 1 is stalled (`grant_m1=0`, `conflict=1`).

#### Module interface
```systemverilog

    input  logic       req_m0,
    input  logic       dest_m0,
    input  logic [7:0] wdata_m0,
    input  logic       req_m1,
    input  logic       dest_m1,
    input  logic [7:0] wdata_m1,
    output logic       grant_m0,
    output logic       grant_m1,
    output logic       bank0_en,
    output logic [7:0] bank0_data,
    output logic       bank1_en,
    output logic [7:0] bank1_data,
    output logic       conflict
);
```

- Purely combinational crossbar switch.
- Master 0 always granted if `req_m0=1`: `grant_m0 = req_m0`.
- Conflict occurs when `req_m0 && req_m1 && (dest_m0 == dest_m1)`.
- Master 1 granted if `req_m1 && !conflict`: `grant_m1 = req_m1 && !conflict`.
- Bank 0 receives data from Master 0 if granted and `dest_m0==0`; else from Master 1 if granted and `dest_m1==0`.
- Bank 1 receives data similarly for destination 1.
- Inactive bank outputs enable=0, data=0.

#### Notes

title: Fix: Register File RAW Hazard Write Forwarding Logic

A 4-register file supports 1 write port (`we, waddr [1:0], wdata [7:0]`) and 1 read port (`raddr [1:0]`).   - Else: return `rf[raddr]`.

title: Fix: Asynchronous FIFO Gray Pointer Empty Comparison Bug

title: Implement the timing: Dual-Port RAM Read-During-Write Pipeline Trace
description:
### Problem statement
A dual-port block memory model operates with 1-cycle synchronous read latency. On write port A (`we_a, addr_a [2:0], din_a [7:0]`), writes complete on posedge clk. On read port B (`re_b, addr_b [2:0]`), registered output `dout_b [7:0]` reflects memory data one cycle later. If `re_b && we_a && (addr_a == addr_b)` (same-cycle collision):
- If `mode_write_first=1`: `dout_b` receives the newly written `din_a` on the next clock.
- If `mode_write_first=0`: `dout_b` receives the pre-existing old memory contents on the next clock.

Implement the dual-port memory timing model exactly according to this cycle contract.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       mode_write_first,
    input  logic       we_a,
    input  logic [2:0] addr_a,
    input  logic [7:0] din_a,
    input  logic       re_b,
    input  logic [2:0] addr_b,
    output logic [7:0] dout_b,
    output logic       collision_warn
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register memory array of eight 8-bit words.
- Output `collision_warn <= re_b && we_a && (addr_a == addr_b)` registered on posedge clk.
- Output `dout_b` registered on posedge clk according to collision mode:
  - If collision and `mode_write_first=1`: `dout_b <= din_a`.
  - Else if `re_b`: `dout_b <= mem[addr_b]`.
  - Else: hold previous `dout_b`.
- Write Port A executes: if `we_a`: `mem[addr_a] <= din_a`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers and outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Accurate memory latency modeling avoids subtle off-by-one verification mismatches.

title: Implement the timing: SDRAM Bank State Precharge Timing Generator
description:
### Problem statement
An SDRAM bank controller enforces a minimum precharge delay `tRP=3` cycles and minimum activate-to-read/write delay `tRCD=2` cycles. When command `cmd_precharge=1`, the controller transitions to `PRECHARGING` and counts 3 clock cycles before asserting `ready_act=1`. When `cmd_activate=1` while ready, the controller transitions to `ACTIVATING` and counts 2 clock cycles before asserting `ready_rw=1`. If an illegal command arrives during a busy timer, `timing_violation` pulses high for 1 cycle.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_trace_sdram_timing(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic cmd_precharge,
    input  logic cmd_activate,
    output logic ready_act,
    output logic ready_rw,
    output logic timing_violation,
    output logic [1:0] state_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- States (2'd0: IDLE, 2'd1: PRE, 2'd2: ACT, 2'd3: OPEN).
- In IDLE: `ready_act=1, ready_rw=0`. If `cmd_precharge`: go to PRE, timer=3.
- In PRE: decrement timer each cycle. When timer reaches 0, go to IDLE (`ready_act=1`).
  - If `cmd_activate` while timer > 0: `timing_violation=1`.
- In IDLE / OPEN: if `cmd_activate`: go to ACT, timer=2.
- In ACT: decrement timer. When timer reaches 0, go to OPEN (`ready_rw=1, ready_act=0`).
  - If `cmd_precharge` or `cmd_activate` while timer > 0: `timing_violation=1`.
- In OPEN: if `cmd_precharge`: go to PRE, timer=3.
- `rst_n` resets to IDLE, outputs 0 (`ready_act=1`).

#### Notes
Hardware timers enforce JEDEC dynamic memory physical recovery constraints.

    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic cmd_precharge,

    output logic timing_violation,
    output logic [1:0] state_out
);

endmodule
solution_hints: Maintain an internal countdown timer for precharge (3 cycles) and activate (2 cycles).
Assert timing_violation if an illegal activation occurs before tRP has expired.
Update state_out to reflect IDLE, PRE, ACT, and OPEN states.

title: Checker: AXI4-Lite Write Address Channel Protocol Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
In the ARM AMBA AXI4-Lite protocol specification, once a master asserts `awvalid=1`, it is strictly forbidden from deasserting `awvalid` until the slave provides `awready=1` (rule A3.2.1). Furthermore, the address payload `awaddr [7:0]` must remain stable and unchanging while stalled (`awvalid && !awready`).

Implement an inline protocol checker that asserts `err_premature_drop` if `awvalid` drops before handshake, and asserts `err_payload_changed` if `awaddr` mutates while stalled.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_chk_axilite_aw(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       awvalid,
    input  logic       awready,
    input  logic [7:0] awaddr,
    output logic       err_premature_drop,
    output logic       err_payload_changed,
    output logic       handshake_count
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register previous `awvalid` and `awaddr` values.
- If previous cycle had `awvalid && !awready`:
  - If current cycle `!awvalid`: assert `err_premature_drop=1`.
  - If current cycle `awaddr != prev_awaddr`: assert `err_payload_changed=1`.
- Output `handshake_count` pulses 1 whenever `awvalid && awready`.
- Reset clears error flags to 0.

#### Notes
Protocol assertion checkers catch subtle bus deadlock bugs during simulation and formal verification.

If awvalid was high and awready was low, awvalid must stay high.

title: Checker: Synchronous FIFO Overflow and Underflow Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
Storage element integrity requires monitoring FIFO push and pop operations against boundary limits. Given current occupancy `depth [3:0]` (capacity 8), push request `push`, and pop request `pop`:
- If `push && (depth == 8) && !pop`: push causes overflow (`overflow_pulse=1`).
- If `pop && (depth == 0)`: pop causes underflow (`underflow_pulse=1`).
- A sticky error register `sticky_err` asserts when either overflow or underflow occurs, remaining high until cleared by `clear_err=1`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_chk_fifo_bounds(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] depth,
    input  logic       push,
    input  logic       pop,
    input  logic       clear_err,
    output logic       overflow_pulse,
    output logic       underflow_pulse,
    output logic       sticky_err
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational error pulses:
  - `overflow_pulse = push && (depth == 4'd8) && !pop`.
  - `underflow_pulse = pop && (depth == 4'd0)`.
- Synchronous `sticky_err` register:
  - Set to 1 if `overflow_pulse || underflow_pulse`.
  - Cleared to 0 if `clear_err=1` (unless a new violation occurs on same cycle).
- `rst_n` clears `sticky_err` to 0.

#### Notes
Sticky error flags latch ephemeral bus corruption events for post-mortem diagnostics.

title: Four-Stage Arithmetic Pipeline with RAW Hazard Stall Interlock
description:
### Problem statement
A 4-stage arithmetic datapath (Fetch, Decode, Execute, Writeback) evaluates sequential operations. When instruction in Decode reads a register (`src_reg [1:0]`) that is currently being modified by an unfinished instruction in Execute (`dest_ex [1:0] && val_ex`), a load-use hazard occurs. The interlock unit must assert `stall_req=1`, freezing the Decode stage and inserting an invalid bubble (`val_ex <= 0`) into the Execute register for 1 clock cycle.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_pipe4_stall(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       val_in,
    input  logic [1:0] src_reg,
    input  logic [1:0] dst_in,
    input  logic [7:0] data_in,
    output logic       stall_req,
    output logic       val_wb,
    output logic [1:0] dst_wb,
    output logic [7:0] data_wb
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 3-stage pipeline registers from Decode to Execute to Writeback.
- RAW Hazard detection: `hazard = val_in && ex_val && (src_reg == ex_dst)`.
- When `hazard=1`: assert `stall_req=1` combinationally.
- Pipeline advancement on posedge clk:
  - If `hazard=1`: bubble inserted into Execute (`ex_val <= 0`), Decode holds its instruction.
  - If `hazard=0`: Execute stage receives inputs from Decode.
  - Writeback stage always advances from Execute.
- `rst_n` clears pipeline registers and outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Hardware interlock stalls protect datapath integrity when operand bypassing is unavailable.

Assert stall_req combinationally when src_reg matches destination of an active stage.
When stalled, clear the execute stage valid bit to inject a bubble.

title: 2D Image Convolution Sliding Window Buffer
description:
### Problem statement
A 2D spatial filtering accelerator processes streaming pixels. For a 4-pixel-wide line raster, the window generator shifts 3 consecutive pixels across 2 internal line buffers to output a 3-tap vertical column `win_col0, win_col1, win_col2 [7:0]`. When `pixel_val=1`, new pixel `pixel_in [7:0]` enters line buffer 0, the tapped pixel from line 0 enters line buffer 1, and the current 3-pixel vertical slice is presented on the outputs.

```systemverilog
module sv_x_conv2d_linebuf(
```

title: Token Bucket Traffic Shaper with Burst Limiting
description:
### Problem statement
A network traffic shaper polices incoming packets using the token-bucket algorithm. Every cycle, `refill_rate [3:0]` tokens are added to the bucket (capped at `max_bucket = 15`). When an incoming packet arrives with `pkt_req=1` and `pkt_len [3:0]`, the shaper permits transmission (`pass=1`) if bucket >= `pkt_len`, decrementing tokens by `pkt_len`. If tokens are insufficient, the packet is rejected/dropped (`drop=1`), and token count remains unchanged.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_token_bucket(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] refill_rate,
    input  logic       pkt_req,
    input  logic [3:0] pkt_len,
    output logic       pass,
    output logic       drop,
    output logic [3:0] token_count
);
```

#### Requirements
- Internal register `tokens` (0..15), initialized to 0 on reset.
- On posedge clk:
  - Refill: intermediate tokens = min(15, `tokens + refill_rate`).
  - If `pkt_req=1`:
    - If intermediate tokens >= `pkt_len`: `pass <= 1, drop <= 0, tokens <= intermediate - pkt_len`.
    - Else: `pass <= 0, drop <= 1, tokens <= intermediate`.
  - Else: `pass <= 0, drop <= 0, tokens <= intermediate`.
- Output `token_count` reflects registered tokens.
- `rst_n` clears all registers and outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Token-bucket shapers enforce sustained average bandwidth while permitting controlled bursts.

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] refill_rate,

    output logic       pass,
    output logic       drop,
    output logic [3:0] token_count
);

endmodule

Clamp maximum accumulated tokens to 15.
Register pass, drop, and updated tokens on posedge clk.

title: Galois Field GF(256) Byte Multiplier by Constant Alpha
description:
### Problem statement
In Reed-Solomon codes and AES Galois counter mode, multiplying a byte `data_in [7:0]` by primitive element $\alpha$ (equivalent to shifting left by 1 in polynomial representation) requires reducing by irreducible polynomial $P(x) = x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1$ (0x11B) whenever the MSB is 1.

Implement the GF(256) multiply-by-2 slice (`xtimes`): if bit 7 is 0, output is `data_in << 1`. If bit 7 is 1, output is `(data_in << 1) ^ 8'h1B`. Both combinational reduction and registered output are provided.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_gf256_mul(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [7:0] data_in,
    output logic [7:0] prod_comb,
    output logic [7:0] prod_reg
);
```

#### Requirements
- Combinational output `prod_comb`:
  - If `data_in[7] == 0`: `prod_comb = data_in << 1`.
  - If `data_in[7] == 1`: `prod_comb = (data_in << 1) ^ 8'h1b`.
- Synchronous register `prod_reg <= prod_comb` on posedge clk.
- `rst_n` clears `prod_reg` to 0.

#### Notes
Finite field arithmetic underpins error-correcting codes and symmetric ciphers.
solution_hints: Check the MSB (data_in[7]) to determine whether polynomial modulo reduction is needed.
Perform left shift by 1 bit, keeping the lower 8 bits.
XOR with 8'h1b when MSB was 1.

title: Fix: Pipeline Stage Valid Stall Latching Bug
description:
### Problem statement
In an elastic pipeline stage, when downstream asserts `stall=1`, the current pipeline stage must retain its valid data (`stage_val` and `stage_data [7:0]`) without dropping or corrupting it. The original code has a bug: when `stall=1`, it unconditionally clears `stage_val <= 0` instead of holding it, causing data loss.

Fix the module so that when `stall=1`, `stage_val` and `stage_data` hold their values; when `stall=0`, the stage loads `in_val` and `in_data`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_fix_pipe_valid_stall(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       stall,
    input  logic       in_val,
    input  logic [7:0] in_data,
    output logic       stage_val,
    output logic [7:0] stage_data
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous pipeline register on posedge clk.
- If `stall == 1`: hold `stage_val` and `stage_data`.
- If `stall == 0`: `stage_val <= in_val`, `stage_data <= in_data`.
- `rst_n` clears `stage_val` and `stage_data` to 0.

#### Notes
Backpressure handling requires freezing register updates rather than clearing valid bits.
solution_hints: Check the stall condition before loading new data.
When stall is high, do nothing to preserve current stage state.
Advance registers only when stall is low.

title: Fix: Three-Sample Digital Glitch Filter Reset Initialization
description:
### Problem statement
A 3-sample digital majority filter debounces an asynchronous button input `raw_btn`. It samples `raw_btn` into a 3-bit history register `hist [2:0]`. The filtered output `btn_clean` asserts if at least 2 out of 3 samples are high (majority 1), and deasserts if at least 2 are low. In the existing code, the reset branch failed to clear the history shift register, allowing lingering uninitialized values to corrupt initial samples.

Fix the module so `hist` and `btn_clean` are reliably cleared to 0 on asynchronous reset `rst_n`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_fix_glitch_filter(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic raw_btn,
    output logic btn_clean,
    output logic [2:0] sample_hist
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 3-bit history register: `hist <= {hist[1:0], raw_btn}`.
- Majority voting: `maj = (hist[0] & hist[1]) | (hist[1] & hist[2]) | (hist[0] & hist[2])`.
- Output `btn_clean <= maj`, `sample_hist = hist`.
- `rst_n` clears `hist` and `btn_clean` to 0.

#### Notes
Majority filtering eliminates high-frequency bounce without requiring analog RC filters.
solution_hints: Clear hist to 3'd0 inside the !rst_n block.
Update hist by shifting in raw_btn at each posedge clk.
Vote across the three sampled history bits.

title: Implement the timing: SPI Quad Read Protocol Cycle State Tracker
description:
### Problem statement
A Quad-SPI Flash read sequence consists of 4 distinct operational phases:
1. Instruction Phase (8 cycles of 1-bit opcode)
2. Address Phase (6 cycles of 4-bit nibbles for 24-bit address)
3. Dummy Wait Phase (4 dummy wait cycles)
4. Data Phase (streaming quad nibbles)

Given chip-select `cs_n` (active low), the module counts SPI clock edges and tracks phase transitions, asserting `phase [1:0]` (0: Inst, 1: Addr, 2: Dummy, 3: Data). When `cs_n=1`, all counters reset to 0.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_trace_spi_qor(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic cs_n,
    output logic [1:0] phase,
    output logic [4:0] phase_cycle,
    output logic       data_valid
);
```

#### Requirements
- When `cs_n=1`: phase <= 0, phase_cycle <= 0, data_valid <= 0.
- When `cs_n=0` on posedge clk:
  - In Phase 0 (Inst): `phase_cycle` counts 0..7. On 7, transition to Phase 1, `phase_cycle <= 0`.
  - In Phase 1 (Addr): `phase_cycle` counts 0..5. On 5, transition to Phase 2, `phase_cycle <= 0`.
  - In Phase 2 (Dummy): `phase_cycle` counts 0..3. On 3, transition to Phase 3, `phase_cycle <= 0`.
  - In Phase 3 (Data): `data_valid <= 1`, `phase_cycle` increments continuously.
- `rst_n` resets all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Quad-SPI phases require cycle-precise tracking of command, address nibbles, and dummy cycles.
solution_hints: Count cycles spent in each phase and advance when reaching terminal counts.
Phase 0 lasts 8 cycles (0..7), Phase 1 lasts 6 cycles (0..5), Phase 2 lasts 4 cycles (0..3).
Clear state whenever cs_n is high.

title: Implement the timing: AXI-Stream Packet Framer with TLAST Assertion
description:
### Problem statement
An AXI4-Stream packet framing engine groups incoming data beats into fixed-length packets of length `pkt_len_bytes [3:0]` (1..15 bytes). When data transfer occurs (`tvalid && tready`), an internal beat counter tracks transferred words. When the beat counter reaches `pkt_len_bytes - 1`, the engine asserts `tlast=1` on that exact cycle to terminate the frame. On the following handshake, the counter resets to 0.

#### Module interface

```systemverilog
module sv_x_trace_axis_packet(

    input  logic       tvalid,
    input  logic       tready,
    input  logic [3:0] pkt_len_bytes,
    output logic       tlast,

);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous counter `beat_count` updated on posedge clk.
- Combinational output `tlast`:
  - Assert `tlast = (beat_count == (pkt_len_bytes - 1'b1))`.
- When `tvalid && tready`:
  - If `tlast`: `beat_count <= 0`.
  - Else: `beat_count <= beat_count + 1`.

Exact TLAST alignment is essential for DMA packet descriptor termination.

Advance beat_count only on valid handshakes (tvalid && tready).
Reset beat_count back to 0 when the last beat completes.

title: Checker: Credit Flow Starvation and Deadlock Timeout Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
In a credit-based network interface, a deadlock occurs if a sender is starved of credits (`credit_val == 0`) while actively attempting to transmit (`tx_pending=1`) for longer than a specified timeout window (`timeout_limit [3:0]`).

Implement an inline runtime checker that monitors this starvation condition. When `tx_pending && (credit_val == 0)`, a starvation counter increments. If the counter reaches `timeout_limit`, output `starvation_alarm` pulses high. If any credit arrives (`credit_ret=1`), the counter resets to 0.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_chk_credit_timeout(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       tx_pending,
    input  logic [3:0] credit_val,
    input  logic       credit_ret,
    input  logic [3:0] timeout_limit,
    output logic       starvation_alarm,
    output logic [3:0] starved_cycles
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous counter `starved_cycles` on posedge clk.
- If `tx_pending && (credit_val == 4'd0)` and `!credit_ret`:
  - If `starved_cycles < timeout_limit`: increment `starved_cycles <= starved_cycles + 1`.
  - If `starved_cycles == timeout_limit`: assert `starvation_alarm <= 1`.
- If `credit_ret || !tx_pending || (credit_val > 0)`: `starved_cycles <= 0, starvation_alarm <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Deadlock detectors expose loss-of-credit bugs before hardware locks permanently.

title: Checker: AXI4-Lite Read Channel Response and Handshake Verifier
description:
### Problem statement
In the ARM AXI4-Lite read channel, every completed read request (`arvalid && arready`) must eventually be followed by a read response (`rvalid && rready`). An inline monitor tracks outstanding read requests (max 4). If `rvalid` asserts when no read was requested, `err_unexpected_resp` asserts. If `rresp == 2'b10` (SLVERR) or `2'b11` (DECERR), `err_slverr` pulses high.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_chk_axilite_rresp(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       ar_hs,
    input  logic       r_hs,
    input  logic [1:0] rresp,
    output logic       err_unexpected_resp,
    output logic       err_slverr,
    output logic [2:0] outstanding_reads
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register `outstanding_reads` (0..4) on posedge clk.
- When `ar_hs && !r_hs`: `outstanding_reads <= outstanding_reads + 1`.
- When `r_hs && !ar_hs && (outstanding_reads > 0)`: `outstanding_reads <= outstanding_reads - 1`.
- Violations:
  - If `r_hs && (outstanding_reads == 0)`: `err_unexpected_resp <= 1`.
  - Else: `err_unexpected_resp <= 0`.
  - If `r_hs && (rresp[1] == 1'b1)`: `err_slverr <= 1`.
  - Else: `err_slverr <= 0`.
- `rst_n` resets all counts and flags to 0.

#### Notes
Tracking in-flight transactions ensures strict request-to-response parity.

    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       ar_hs,

    output logic       err_unexpected_resp,
    output logic       err_slverr,
    output logic [2:0] outstanding_reads
);

endmodule
solution_hints: Maintain outstanding_reads counter, incremented by ar_hs and decremented by r_hs.
Flag err_unexpected_resp when r_hs occurs while outstanding_reads is zero.
Flag err_slverr whenever rresp MSB is asserted (SLVERR or DECERR).

title: Circular Event Trace Buffer with Overwrite Protection
description:
### Problem statement
An on-chip diagnostic flight recorder logs hardware events into an 8-entry circular buffer. When `log_val=1`, event data `event_in [7:0]` is written to `wr_ptr [2:0]`. When all 8 entries are filled, `wrapped_flag` asserts. If `allow_overwrite=1`, logging continues, overwriting old entries; if `allow_overwrite=0`, logging freezes (`frozen=1`) and new events are dropped.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_trace_log_buf(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       allow_overwrite,
    input  logic       log_val,
    input  logic [7:0] event_in,
    output logic [2:0] wr_ptr,
    output logic       wrapped_flag,
    output logic       frozen,
    output logic [7:0] last_logged
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous write pointer `wr_ptr` (0..7) on posedge clk.
- On `log_val=1`:
  - If not frozen:
    - `last_logged <= event_in`.
    - `wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1`.
    - If `wr_ptr == 7`:
      - `wrapped_flag <= 1`.

title: Iterative Bit-by-Bit Integer Square Root Engine
description:

A 4-step sequential integer square root engine calculates $\lfloor\sqrt{x}\rfloor$ and remainder $r = x - q^2$ for an 8-bit radicand `radicand [7:0]`. When `start=1`, the engine latches `radicand`, asserts `busy=1`, and processes 2 bits of radicand per step (4 iterations total). title: Cascaded Two-Digit BCD Stopwatch with Lap Freeze Register
description:
### Problem statement
A digital stopwatch displays tenths-of-seconds (`bcd_tenths [3:0]`, 0..9) and seconds (`bcd_ones [3:0]`, 0..9). When `run=1`, `bcd_tenths` increments every cycle. When tenths rolls from 9 to 0, `bcd_ones` increments. When ones rolls from 9 to 0, both wrap to 0. When `lap=1`, internal counting continues uninterrupted, but the output registers freeze to display the captured lap time until `lap=0`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_bcd_stopwatch(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       run,
    input  logic       lap,
    output logic [3:0] disp_tenths,
    output logic [3:0] disp_ones,
    output logic       wrap_second
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous internal BCD counters `cnt_tenths` and `cnt_ones` on posedge clk.
- When `run=1`:
  - If `cnt_tenths == 9`: `cnt_tenths <= 0`; if `cnt_ones == 9`: `cnt_ones <= 0`; else `cnt_ones <= cnt_ones + 1`.
  - Else: `cnt_tenths <= cnt_tenths + 1`.
- Output `wrap_second <= (run && (cnt_tenths == 9))` registered.
- Display multiplexing:
  - If `lap=0`: `disp_tenths <= cnt_tenths, disp_ones <= cnt_ones`.
  - If `lap=1`: hold previous frozen display registers.
- `rst_n` clears all counters and display registers to 0.

#### Notes
Decoupled display registers permit continuous background timing during lap readouts.

    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       run,

    output logic [3:0] disp_ones,
    output logic       wrap_second

Cascade cnt_ones whenever cnt_tenths rolls over from 9 to 0.

title: Direct Digital Synthesizer Phase Accumulator with Quadrant Mapping
description:
### Problem statement
A Direct Digital Synthesizer (DDS) Numerically Controlled Oscillator (NCO) produces a sinusoidal phase trajectory. A 16-bit phase accumulator increments by frequency tuning word `ftw [15:0]` on each clock edge: `phase_acc <= phase_acc + ftw`. The upper 2 bits of `phase_acc` define the current quadrant `quadrant [1:0]`, the next 6 bits provide the ROM lookup address `lut_addr [5:0]`, and `msb_square` provides a 50% duty-cycle square wave.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_dds_phase_acc(
    input  logic        clk,
    input  logic        rst_n,
    input  logic        enable,
    input  logic [15:0] ftw,
    output logic [15:0] phase_out,
    output logic [1:0]  quadrant,
    output logic [5:0]  lut_addr,
    output logic        msb_square
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 16-bit register `phase_acc` on posedge clk.
- When `enable=1`: `phase_acc <= phase_acc + ftw`.
- When `enable=0`: hold `phase_acc`.
- Combinational outputs:
  - `phase_out = phase_acc`.
  - `quadrant = phase_acc[15:14]`.
  - `lut_addr = phase_acc[13:8]`.
  - `msb_square = phase_acc[15]`.
- `rst_n` clears `phase_acc` to 0.

#### Notes
DDS architecture yields sub-Hertz frequency tuning resolution at zero phase discontinuity.

    input  logic        clk,
    input  logic        rst_n,
    input  logic        enable,

    output logic [1:0]  quadrant,
    output logic [5:0]  lut_addr,
    output logic        msb_square
);

endmodule
solution_hints: Accumulate ftw into phase_acc on every enabled clock cycle.

title: Fix: Circular Ring Buffer Read Pointer Modulo Boundary Bug
description:
### Problem statement
A 16-entry ring buffer tracks its read tail pointer `tail_ptr [3:0]`. When read strobe `pop=1` occurs while buffer is non-empty (`not_empty=1`), `tail_ptr` increments modulo 16. In the buggy code, the designer erroneously wrapped the pointer when `tail_ptr == 14` instead of allowing it to reach 15, skipping element 15 entirely and causing silent data corruption.

Fix the module so `tail_ptr` increments through all 16 entries (0..15) cleanly.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_fix_circ_buf_wrap(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       pop,
    input  logic       not_empty,
    output logic [3:0] tail_ptr,
    output logic       wrap_pulse
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 4-bit pointer `tail_ptr` on posedge clk.
- When `pop && not_empty`:
  - `tail_ptr <= tail_ptr + 1` (natural 4-bit modular rollover 0..15).
- `wrap_pulse` asserts for 1 cycle when `pop && not_empty && (tail_ptr == 15)`.
- `rst_n` clears `tail_ptr` and `wrap_pulse` to 0.

#### Notes
Off-by-one pointer wraps in circular buffers lead to data corruption that evades simple unit tests.
solution_hints: Allow tail_ptr to count up to 15 before rolling over to 0.
Assert wrap_pulse only when tail_ptr is currently 15 and pop occurs.
Reset both signals to 0 on asynchronous reset.

title: Fix: 8-Bit Galois LFSR Feedback Polynomial Tap Application Bug
description:
### Problem statement
An 8-bit Galois Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) with characteristic polynomial $x^8 + x^6 + x^5 + x^4 + 1$ (mask 8'h71) shifts right each cycle. If the departing LSB (`lfsr[0]`) is 1, the new state is `(lfsr >> 1) ^ 8'h71` with MSB set. If LSB is 0, the state is simply `(lfsr >> 1)`. The original designer XORed the mask into the unshifted register before checking LSB, producing an invalid pseudo-random sequence.

Fix the module so the Galois reduction step is correctly executed.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_fix_galois_lfsr(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       enable,
    output logic [7:0] lfsr_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 8-bit register `lfsr` on posedge clk.
- When `enable=1`:
  - If `lfsr[0] == 1`: `lfsr <= (lfsr >> 1) ^ 8'h8e` (tap mask 8'b10001110 = 8'h8e applied with MSB set).
  - Else: `lfsr <= (lfsr >> 1)`.
- On reset `rst_n=0`: seed with `8'hA5`.

#### Notes
Galois LFSRs place XOR gates in parallel between flip-flops, enabling much higher clock speeds than Fibonacci topologies.
solution_hints: Initialize lfsr to 8'hA5 on reset.
Check lfsr[0] to determine whether to XOR with 8'h8e.
Right-shift by 1 bit and XOR if LSB was 1.

title: Implement the timing: Non-Overlapping Two-Phase Clock Generator with Dead Time
description:
### Problem statement
Custom dynamic CMOS circuits and switched-capacitor filters require two non-overlapping clock phases, $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$, with a guaranteed dead time where both phases remain low to avoid crowbar currents. Given a 4-cycle period modulo counter (0..3):
- State 0: $\phi_1=1, \phi_2=0$ (Phase 1 active)
- State 1: $\phi_1=0, \phi_2=0$ (Dead-time gap)
- State 2: $\phi_1=0, \phi_2=1$ (Phase 2 active)
- State 3: $\phi_1=0, \phi_2=0$ (Dead-time gap)

Generate registered outputs `phi1`, `phi2`, and `dead_time` matching this timing sequence.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_trace_two_phase_clk(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic enable,
    output logic phi1,
    output logic phi2,
    output logic dead_time,
    output logic [1:0] step
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 2-bit counter `step` (0..3) on posedge clk.
- When `enable=1`: `step <= step + 1`.
- Outputs registered on posedge clk:
  - `phi1 <= enable && (step == 2'd3)` (next step is 0).

title: Implement the timing: Safe Glitchless Clock Mux with Intermediate Park State
description:
### Problem statement
When switching between asynchronous clock sources or bus masters (`sel [1:0]`), glitch-free operation requires first disabling the active source into a neutral 'parked' state for 1 intermediate cycle before enabling the newly selected source. If `target_sel != cur_sel`, the controller asserts `parking=1` and drives output `mux_out=0` for 1 clock cycle before switching to `target_sel`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_trace_mux_park(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [1:0] sel_in,
    input  logic [7:0] in0,
    input  logic [7:0] in1,
    input  logic [7:0] in2,
    output logic [7:0] mux_out,
    output logic [1:0] active_sel,
    output logic       parking
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous controller on posedge clk.
- If `sel_in != active_sel` and `!parking`:
  - Assert `parking <= 1`, `mux_out <= 8'd0`.
- If `parking==1`:
  - `parking <= 0`, `active_sel <= sel_in`.
  - Route corresponding input to `mux_out` (0->in0, 1->in1, 2->in2).
- If `sel_in == active_sel` and `!parking`:
  - Continuously update `mux_out` with selected input.
- `rst_n` resets `active_sel=0`, `mux_out=0`, `parking=0`.

#### Notes
Parking clock muxes avoids glitches and runt clock pulses during dynamic frequency scaling.

title: Checker: Peripheral Bus Write Strobe Minimum Pulse Width Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
A legacy asynchronous peripheral bus specification mandates that the active-high write strobe `wr_strobe` must remain asserted high for a minimum duration of 2 consecutive clock cycles (`min_width = 2`). If `wr_strobe` pulses high for only 1 cycle and drops low on the next, a narrow-pulse timing violation occurs. Output `err_pulse_too_narrow` must assert high for 1 cycle.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_chk_bus_strobe(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic wr_strobe,
    output logic err_pulse_too_narrow,
    output logic [1:0] strobe_len
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous counter `strobe_len` (0..3) on posedge clk.
- When `wr_strobe=1`: `strobe_len <= (strobe_len < 3) ? (strobe_len + 1) : strobe_len`.
- When `wr_strobe=0`:
  - If `strobe_len == 1`: assert `err_pulse_too_narrow <= 1`.
  - Else: `err_pulse_too_narrow <= 0`.
  - `strobe_len <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
Monitoring minimum pulse width prevents setup/hold violations on slower peripheral register banks.
solution_hints: Increment strobe_len during cycles where wr_strobe remains high.
When wr_strobe falls, check if strobe_len was only 1.
Assert err_pulse_too_narrow when the pulse duration was fewer than 2 cycles.

title: Checker: Dual-Region Memory Protection Unit Access Boundary Guard
description:
### Problem statement
A hardware Memory Protection Unit (MPU) guards privileged address spaces. Two programmable protected regions are defined: Region 0 (`[base0..limit0]`) and Region 1 (`[base1..limit1]`). When memory transaction `req=1` occurs with target address `addr [7:0]`, the MPU verifies access permissions: if `privileged_mode=0` (user mode) and `addr` falls within either protected region (`(addr >= base0 && addr <= limit0) || (addr >= base1 && addr <= limit1)`), an access fault occurs (`fault=1`, `grant=0`). Privileged accesses (`privileged_mode=1`) or accesses outside protected regions proceed normally (`grant=1`, `fault=0`).

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sv_x_chk_mpu_range(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       req,
    input  logic       privileged_mode,
    input  logic [7:0] addr,
    input  logic [7:0] base0,
    input  logic [7:0] limit0,
    input  logic [7:0] base1,
    input  logic [7:0] limit1,
    output logic       grant,
    output logic       fault,
    output logic       sticky_fault
);
```

#### Requirements
- Region bounds check: `in_r0 = (addr >= base0 && addr <= limit0)`, `in_r1 = (addr >= base1 && addr <= limit1)`.
- Access rule: violation occurs if `req && !privileged_mode && (in_r0 || in_r1)`.
- Combinational outputs:
  - `fault = violation`.
  - `grant = req && !violation`.
- Synchronous `sticky_fault` on posedge clk latches 1 on any fault until reset.
- `rst_n` clears `sticky_fault` to 0.

#### Notes
Hardware memory protection prevents user-space processes from tampering with kernel space or device registers.
